justification: Changes the write path of the applicability tagger and adds two production columns to regulatory_provisions (55,696 rows). Additive and nullable, but it touches the field behind the hard zone filter in for-property/route.ts, so a regression would mis-serve provisions.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: _resolve stops distinguishing the four outcomes (a stub returning a constant fails either the asserted or the defaulted cases), tag() stops returning exactly two values, the validity-gate rejection stops being distinct from never-found, or APPLICABILITY_SOURCES drifts from the CHECK constraint in migration 062. Separately verified against production: an out-of-vocabulary value is REJECTED by the constraint and a valid one accepted (both rolled back), so the CHECK is not decoration.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions had 65 columns / 55,696 rows before; 67 after. Measured 2026-08-01: 19,072 of 19,957 served rows (95.6%) carry ALL for both zones and dev types with no record of why. The tagger returned ALL from seven distinct code paths, all writing the identical value.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed ALL mostly meant a mis-tag. It does not - a falsifiable probe found only 0.50% demonstrably zone-specific. The defect is that ALL is UNATTRIBUTABLE, not that it is wrong, so the fix records provenance and changes no tag value.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No existing column or table records tagger provenance (checked the regulatory_provisions column list directly). The constrained-vocabulary plus DB CHECK pattern is copied from control_type_vocabulary.py rather than invented. tag() keeps its two-value contract; provenance arrives via a new tag_with_provenance().

functions.name: _resolve
functions.input: a config entry dict or None, plus one applicability key name
functions.output: a tuple of the resolved list and the source label explaining where that list came from
functions.if_none: a None or empty entry returns ALL with source no_config, never implying a decision was made

functions.name: _from_entry
functions.input: a config entry plus optional site conditions and extra keys
functions.output: the config result dict now carrying zone_source and dev_type_source beside the values
functions.if_none: a None entry still returns a well formed dict whose two sources both read no_config

functions.name: tag_with_provenance
functions.input: provision text, document id, and the optional valid zone set for that LGA
functions.output: zones, dev types, and a dict of the two source labels drawn from the closed vocabulary
functions.if_none: with no document id the sources read no_document_id rather than a label implying a config decided

values: N/A - no business values are read; the change records provenance for values already computed.

queries.purpose: persist the two provenance labels alongside the tags during a retag run
queries.where_clause: WHERE id = %s - single row by primary key, inside the existing batched retag loop which already scopes on v2_applicable_zones IS NULL

break_it.scenario: The provenance column is added but every row gets the same label, so it looks populated and answers nothing.
break_it.what_happens: Four outcomes are asserted mutually distinct; a constant-returning stub fails either the asserted or the defaulted half.
break_it.how: Explicit test that the four labels collapse to no fewer than four distinct values.

break_it.scenario: Old rows are backfilled with a guessed source, fabricating the very fact the column exists to record.
break_it.what_happens: The migration contains no UPDATE. Existing rows stay NULL, documented as unknown-origin and explicitly not a pass.
break_it.how: test_migration_does_not_backfill asserts no UPDATE statement exists in the migration.

break_it.scenario: The Python vocabulary and the DB CHECK drift, so the pipeline writes a label the database rejects at 3am.
break_it.what_happens: Every member of APPLICABILITY_SOURCES is asserted present in the migration SQL, and the constraint was verified live to reject an unknown value.
break_it.how: test_every_source_appears_in_the_migration plus a live accept/reject probe against production, both rolled back.

break_it.scenario: Adding a third return value breaks every existing caller of tag().
break_it.what_happens: tag() still returns exactly two values and delegates to tag_with_provenance; both are asserted to agree on the values.
break_it.how: TestBackwardCompatibility pins the arity and the value agreement across three shapes of input.

break_it.scenario: A zone code found then rejected as invalid for the LGA looks identical to one never found, hiding that a bad code was caught.
break_it.what_happens: The validity gate sets filtered_to_all, distinct from no_config and excluded from TRUSTED_ALL_SOURCES.

break_it.scenario: The migration runs against production and damages the 55,696 existing rows.
break_it.what_happens: Purely additive DDL with IF NOT EXISTS throughout, no UPDATE, no DROP, no CASCADE. Verified live: 55,696 rows before and after, both columns nullable, zero rows populated.
break_it.how: test_migration_is_additive_only blocks DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE/CASCADE in the file; row count compared before and after the real run.

break_it.scenario: A blanket string replace matches an 8-space `return` inside a 12-space line, dedenting it to method level and making every branch below unreachable.
break_it.what_happens: It happened. Marrickville Part 1 and Part 3 silently fell through to no_config/ALL. The full 3,332-test suite stayed GREEN because nothing exercised those two parts; a GPT-5.6 cross-review found it. Fixed, and a parametrised reachability test now covers all five Marrickville parts.
break_it.how: The guard asserts on SOURCE not value: Part 1 legitimately resolves to ALL, so asserting zones==['ALL'] would have passed while broken. Mutation-verified — re-dedenting the return fails exactly the Part 1 and Part 3 cases.

break_it.scenario: The migration's idempotency guard checks pg_constraint by NAME only, so a same-named constraint on any other table makes a re-run skip the CHECK and leave the column ungated.
break_it.what_happens: conname is unique per (table, name), not globally. Raised by cross-review; the guard is now scoped with conrelid = 'public.regulatory_provisions'::regclass.
break_it.how: Scoped predicate added. The constraint already exists correctly on the right table in production, so this only affects future re-runs.

post_merge.db_reset: None. Migration 062 is already applied to production and is additive. Rollback if ever needed: ALTER TABLE regulatory_provisions DROP COLUMN v2_zone_source, DROP COLUMN v2_dev_type_source.
post_merge.manual_verify: The columns are live but every row is NULL until a retag runs. run_applicability_tagging only revisits rows WHERE v2_applicable_zones IS NULL, so a full-corpus retag is a separate, user-approved operation. Until then the honest reading of the corpus is unchanged: 95.6% ALL, origin unknown.
